title: Pinch pot miniature teacup set
subtitle: Making four tiny air-dry clay teacups with handles and saucers from pinched clay
excerpt: Four miniature teacups , each about 50 mm tall , and matching saucers are pinched and shaped from air-dry clay. The handles are thin clay ropes attached with slip. The set is a good pinch-pot exercise because the small scale reveals any wall thickness inconsistency and the matching shapes train your eye and hand to produce consistent results.
sourceNotes: Miniature teacup set in air-dry clay derived from first principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: A pot formed by pressing a thumb into a ball of clay and pinching the walls thin between thumb and fingers
Roughening clay surfaces with a needle and applying diluted clay before joining two pieces
The ideal stage for attaching handles: the cup wall holds its shape without support

content.text: A miniature
pinch pot

teacup is a compact exercise in consistent hand pressure. Making four in sequence trains your hands to repeat the same movement, which is the most direct way to improve at pinching. The saucers are simple flat discs , quick to make and useful as a scale reference throughout.
Make the cups
Divide 250 g of clay into four equal balls, about 60 g each. Weigh them if you want matched cups.

For each ball: push a thumb into the centre to within 5 mm of the base. Pinch the wall by pressing the clay between thumb and forefinger, rotating the ball a little with each pinch. Work from the base upward, keeping walls 4-5 mm thick throughout.
Target a finished height of 45-50 mm and a rim diameter of 50-55 mm. Flatten the base on the work surface by pressing gently , the cup should stand without wobbling.
Smooth the outside of each cup with a damp sponge. Smooth the inside with a fingertip. Align the rims by turning each cup upside down and gently pressing the rim on the work surface to level it.
Make and attach the handles
Allow the cups to reach
leather-hard
before attaching handles. This takes 1-2 hours at room temperature.
Roll four handles , thin clay ropes about 5 mm diameter and 50 mm long. Curve each into a D shape and allow to stiffen slightly.
On each cup, mark two attachment points on the outer wall 25-30 mm apart vertically.
Score and slip
both the marked spots and the handle ends. Press the handle ends firmly onto the cup and smooth the join with a damp finger.
Make the saucers

Divide the remaining 100 g of clay into four 25 g pieces. Roll each into a flat disc 8 mm thick and about 70 mm diameter. Smooth the edges and create a very shallow central indent about 35 mm across for the cup to sit in.
Dry, paint, and seal
Allow all pieces to dry fully. Paint with two coats of acrylic or coloured slip. A consistent colour across all four cups and saucers unifies the set.
Seal with two coats of PVA varnish. The pieces are decorative , the varnish will protect them from handling but they are not suitable for hot liquid.

items.solution: Weigh the clay before pinching. A consistent starting weight gives you consistent proportions.
The cup was probably still too soft when the handle was attached, or score-and-slip was skipped. Reattach at leather-hard stage using PVA adhesive if the piece is already bone-dry.
